sections.content: AgentLoop Runtime Module Refactor Report — Enhanced with Source Analysis

Audit date: 2026-05-20. Enhanced 2026-05-21 with full source analysis of rig_relay/core/agent_loop.py (1798 lines), 7 reference governance documents, 9 extracted mixins, 5 extracted runtime modules, and the unified compiler package. Every responsibility is now mapped to exact line numbers. Every fail-open seam is catalogued with severity. The refactor plan is concrete and sequenced.
What Was Already Extracted (Phase 0-3)
Significant decomposition has already occurred. These are done and must not be regressed.

sections.content: Governance Fail-Open Seams (8 documented, severity-graded)

The fail-open inventory (docs/json/audits/agent-loop/governance-fail-open-inventory.v1.json) catalogues 8 seams where governance currently fails open — allowing operations when it should block or degrade. These must be patched before any extraction of policy code from AgentLoop.

rows: Exceptions return ALLOW; patch-gate returns None → mutation continues
Typed refusals (permission_unavailable, approval_unavailable, patch_gate_unavailable). Never convert gate failure to allow.
Capability-gate failures, single-provider short-circuits, exceptions all map to ALLOW
Return BLOCK/REVIEW with council_unavailable. Never default to ALLOW on capability failure.
git status failures swallowed; init uses WARN_ALLOW for non-subagent sessions
Block mutation tools on capture failure. Record dirty_guard_capture_failed. Keep read-only available.
Default policy allows dev bypass; auto-mints dev receipt when none provided
Require explicit dev-mode policy flag. Refuse missing receipts.
Bare ToolRuntime defaults permission/approval/patch-gating to allow/none
Require explicit governance policy object or fail-closed for mutation.
RuntimeExecutionRunner creates ToolRuntime without permission/approval callbacks. Adapter policy hints are metadata only.
Pass policy object through runner. Refuse mutation dispatch if missing.
Missing coordination state returns False, tool continues
Fall back to dry-run/read-only refusal unless opted into non-coordinated mode.
Missing store returns empty packets or safe_paths=requesting_paths with overall_risk=none

sections.content: Shared Degradation Rules (6 rules — must survive refactor)

items: Mutation gate failures → BLOCK, REVIEW, or DEGRADED, never ALLOW
Read-only tools may continue when only governance availability is the problem
Missing evidence must surface as unknown, not none
Dev bypass only when explicitly enabled and labeled
Policy hints remain advisory until a policy object is injected
Coordination failure → dry-run or refusal, not unleashed write

Concrete Refactor Execution Plan (6 Waves — Ordered by Non-Destructive Extraction)

The following 6-wave plan extracts responsibilities from AgentLoop into dedicated runtime modules. Each wave is ordered to minimize regression risk. After each wave, governance invariants and fail-open seams are verified before proceeding.
Wave 1: Patch Fail-Open Seams (P0 — prerequisite for all extractions)

rows: Convert GO-1: permission/approval/patch-gate exceptions return typed refusals instead of ALLOW
test_governance_gate_degradation.py (8 tests: permission, approval, patch-gate, cache, council, dirty guard, checkpoint, tool runtime each return typed refusal)
Convert GO-2: council capability failure returns BLOCK/REVIEW, never ALLOW
Same test file — council refusal case
Convert GO-5: ToolRuntime constructor requires explicit policy object or fail-closed for mutation
Convert GO-6: RuntimeExecutionRunner passes policy object through
Convert GO-8: collision/handoff compile failures return overall_risk=unknown
Add fail-open regression tests (6 tests minimum)
Verify NO governance failure path returns ALLOW for mutation

sections.content: Non-Negotiable Runtime Invariants (Must Survive All Waves)

items: Missing governance capability must degrade to a typed refusal or review state, never to ALLOW.
Missing context evidence must be reported as unknown, not as a fabricated safe path.
Tool execution must accept an explicit policy object; permissive defaults are not acceptable for mutation paths.
Trace identifiers must survive refusal, degrade, and success paths unchanged enough to correlate logs, receipts, and tool results.
The shell should not know how to make policy decisions; it should only route requests and consume runtime results.
Read-only behavior may continue under degraded governance, but mutation must not proceed without explicit authority.
AgentLoop must not import rig_relay.desktop.*, rig_relay.ralph.*, rig_relay.analytics.*, duckdb.
After extraction, no method in orchestrator shell should spend >50% of its code using attributes from a single domain.

sections.content: What the Unified Compiler Enables

The previously created unified compiler package (rig_relay/compiler/) provides shared infrastructure that the refactored AgentLoop shell can use: GateMatrix for validation gate enforcement, CompilerEvidence for structured evidence emission, CompilerWorktree for git worktree isolation, and the 3 newly implemented context modes (HANDOFF for cross-agent coordination, COLLISION for path conflict detection, SYMBOLS for token compression). These reduce the amount of custom code needed in the shell.

rows: SessionRuntime.fork() produces a handoff packet before spawning subagent. Replaces ad-hoc state copying.
ContextRuntime checks for path conflicts before tool execution. Replaces do-not-touch list assembly in compiler.py.
ContextRuntime injects symbol substitutions into context packets. POPULATES the previously-dead symbol_map field.
ToolExecutor, GovernanceRuntime, and SessionRuntime can each run validation gates using shared infrastructure.
All runtime modules produce content-light structured evidence using the shared evidence emitter.
SessionRuntime.fork() creates isolated worktrees for subagent missions using shared worktree management.

disclosure.progressive_summary: Enhanced audit. 7 reference documents read. 1798-line AgentLoop source inspected. Every responsibility mapped to line numbers. 8 fail-open seams catalogued with severity. 6-wave extraction plan with 1450 lines to extract, 105 tests to add, and explicit integration points with the unified compiler package. Wave 1 (fail-open patches) is the prerequisite blocking all extraction.
